diagnostic_interpretation: Probe1 reaches ten already-accessed descriptor cases for software INT80 before a cross-wrap A=0 update exits with KVM INTERNAL_ERROR. Probe2 records all four event kinds, retaining every internal exit as a failed test, never as an architectural guest outcome.

Probe2 has 40 valid original observations and 40 direct-owner comparisons per core. All 24 cross-wrap A=0 cases per core, including pre-set leaf A/D controls, exit with KVM INTERNAL_ERROR_SIMUL_EX=2 and interruption info 0x80000b11 (#AC during delivery). Host split-lock settings were not changed. KVM_GET/SET_MSRS reject MSR_TEST_CTRL 0x33 in the disposable capability probe.

Probe3 removes the cross-line update cases and adds aligned high-canonical and last-qword A=0 descriptors with writable/read-only controls. Both cores finish all 56 original observations. P has four canonicality error-frame RAM differences; E has twelve. Both have eight A=0/read-only State differences: original CR2 is the descriptor start, whereas the current byte update reports start+5. These eight per-core cases remain unresolved and are not included among final canonicality passes.
Final canonicality groups use the ten A=1 cases with full represented CPU/RAM comparisons. Descriptor updates are unchanged, not silently replaced by the return instruction qword transaction.

First implementation build attempts failed before tests because inheriting the protected base constructor did not make it publicly callable. Explicit public forwarding constructors fix the access issue; original failed build logs are retained.

native_oracle.method: Fresh KVM VM/vCPU per stream, two initial SREGS writes and no intermediate rewrites. KVM_PRE_FAULT_MEMORY fills physical backing. Four original streams (INT80, INT3, explicit IRQ and NMI) each use ten A=1 descriptor inputs. Full represented State and every byte of 0x40000 RAM are compared without output masks. Original target/debug and HLT code pages are pre-accessed in both inputs; absent-first-wrapped-page ancestors are pre-accessed in both inputs.

profiles.SelectorForStart: Qualified local P core type 0x40: noncanonical start reports selector|EXT, noncanonical tail reports EXT.
profiles.SelectorForRange: Qualified local E core type 0x20: noncanonical start and tail report selector|EXT.

limitations: Only pinned local Intel hybrid cores qualify these choices; no production host inference.
The final matrix has already-accessed descriptors. No new accessed-write width, locked transaction, cache publication or split-lock policy is qualified.
No initially-clear fault-walk ancestor A policy is inferred. Original executions are uninterrupted; backing/budget cases verify software retention contracts against uninterrupted software results.

coverage: Independent code64 software INT/INT3 and explicit IRQ/NMI streams cover low/high canonical extremes, noncanonical start/tail, range-before-paging priority, high canonical page faults, end-to-zero qword wrap and descriptor-base-plus-index wrap.

HighC and LLVMC through host-x64 Clang and NeverC at O0/O2: 320 original/generated comparisons per SDK, plus 40 direct-owner comparisons. Nonzero CR2 distinguishes its preservation on GP from page-fault addresses. External selector errors retain EXT; page-fault error codes are not ORed with EXT.

160 software event-resume comparisons per SDK cover first/mid IDT backing, descriptor backing, partial exception-frame writes and unaccepted secondary events at work-budget stops. Retained NMI acceptance, error codes and instruction budgets survive retries. Changed ordinary-context profile refuses before effects; lower resume uses the token profile.

24 suspended IRET/MOV DS/LGS comparisons preserve the event binding before an instruction faults; four software INT-to-data-DB sequences preserve it after software completion at an unaccepted event-budget stop.

96 full-mode comparisons per SDK keep frozen profiles through backing and budget stops when a reconstructed caller supplies the opposite choice. Unknown direct, ordinary-context and token profiles refuse before effects.

Shared neutral descriptor-range owner performs complete-extent checks before paging. Event binding is independent of selector/return profiles and their accessed-store choices; existing enum numeric identities are unchanged.
boundaries: NeverC remains host/source x64; guest mode/operand widths do not add a compiler target.
Full paged-source, legacy-source, shared events/native paging, low instruction-boundary and SDK suites are replayed on both SDKs. Prior independent paging qualification is not recounted.

Event accessed-update CR2/locked transaction and split-lock qualification remain open, along with mode-aware owners, real/unreal/VM86 composition, software SMM/SGX, unbound asynchronous producers and physical SGX qualification.
Production LLVM remains neverd-llvm-v23.0.0-r6. No LLVM release, production pin or source gitlink change.
